data.narrative:
Stratum AI is a seed-stage climate and energy technology company founded by Daniel Mogilny and Farzi Yusufali, having raised $400K to date. The valuation landscape includes one public comparable (LNZA) and eight private peers in the climate and energy sector, including Redwood Materials, QuantumScape, KoBold Metals, Electric Hydrogen, and Enovix.

Given the early stage and limited data, only the stage-progression method proved applicable. Using total raised ($400K) as a baseline valuation proxy and applying a typical seed-to-next-stage multiplier of 2.5x yields an implied valuation of $1M. A peer-median approach could not be reliably applied due to insufficient same-stage or adjacent-stage comparables within the climate and energy universe; while eight sector peers exist, none met the narrow filtering criteria of stage alignment or valuation-tier similarity necessary for meaningful benchmarking.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $850K to $1.15M, with a median of $1M. This range reflects stage-progression mechanics applied conservatively. The primary valuation uncertainty stems from the absence of transaction data for early-stage climate-tech peers at similar capital levels. Additional clarity on product-market fit, technical differentiation, and pathway to Series A fundraising would meaningfully refine this estimate.
